description:
I sat down with Howard Marks, the co-founder of Oaktree and the man who has been writing the memos every serious investor on earth opens first for over thirty years, and what was supposed to be a conversation about debt and cycles became a conversation about how anyone gets above-average at anything in a world where everyone smart is already trying — we covered why he picked bonds over stocks for an entire career and got rich doing the opposite of what everyone wanted to do, why the S&P returns 10% a year but almost never between 8 and 12, why he changed his mind on AI after a single conversation with Claude, what AI can't do that great investors still can, why he thinks India's biggest export business sits in the crosshairs of AI, and where the $10 bill nobody has picked up is hiding right now.

00:00 Introduction
02:05 From Queens to Wharton beginnings
08:10 Mujo and independence of events
15:17 Why cycles exist in markets
22:09 Pandemic, recessions, and recovery age
28:38 Where we are today
36:08 Drifting versus seeing the river
42:57 Oak Tree and accidental entrepreneurship
49:45 Why bonds over equities
57:14 Distressed bonds and excess returns
1:05:36 Beginning a new career today
1:12:42 Active management versus indexation
1:20:08 Learning from Andrew, second level thinking
1:27:25 How to become contrarian and better
1:34:28 Learning from history, final advice
